And with regard to this incentivization and all, it is already there. As and when these things are coming to us,

guidance.statement: Full year EBITDA margin guided at 15.1% plus 1% upside from operating leverage in H2
guidance.quote: For the full year, I would say we have done 15.1% margin in the H1. With the leverage effect, with H2 being 1.5x to 1.65x of H1, more or less, I expect the same to pan out this year as well. You can say 15% plus upside of 1%.

guidance.statement: Export target of 3 GW order book and 1 GW sales by FY31
guidance.quote: We are looking at 3 gigawatts order book by FY31. We are looking at 1 gigawatts sale by FY31.

guidance.statement: FY27 WTG contribution margin expected at 22-23% range, normalized EBITDA margin 16.5-17% excluding non-recurring costs and commodity/FX impact
guidance.quote: WTG contribution margins are expected to remain in that 22%, 23% range for FY27, is the belief and it should get normalized subject to some of these externalities getting normalized.

guidance.statement: Target 40% India market share by FY31, order book to grow from 6 GW to 15 GW by FY31 exit, annual sales of ~10 GW by FY31, 25% CAGR trajectory
guidance.quote: We have said from our 30%, 33% market share, we wish to increase our India market share to 40%. This we said we will do by FY31. We also mentioned we are looking at our order book from current 6 gigawatts to 15 gigawatts as an exit of FY31.

demand.statement: Industry bid momentum strong with 8-9 GW wind RTC/FDRE tenders awarded in H1 FY27, C&I pipeline robust, annual installations expected to cross 10 GW near term and reach 15 GW by FY31
demand.quote: Bid momentum is also gaining traction, with almost 8 -9 gigawatts of wind RTC, FDRE, wind -dominated tenders being awarded in H1 FY27. C&I pipeline also stands robust. This sets the stage for a multi -year growth cycle, with annual installations expected to cross 10 gigawatts in the near term and reach 15 gigawatts by FY31.

margin.quote: Operating expenses increased by about INR80 crores during Q2 FY27 versus Q2 FY26, largely led by higher Suzlon 2.0 related branding, travel, SG&A related to associated costs, which are around INR50 crores. This is expected to be phased down in subsequent quarters.

order_book.statement: Order book at 6 GW providing 18-month coverage, secured 1.5 GW new orders in H1 FY27, strong pipeline with DevCo model
order_book.quote: Our order book of 6 gigawatts reaffirms our market leadership. In H1 '27, we have already secured 1.5 gigawatts of orders and continue to have strong pipeline. The current order backlog provides coverage for 18 months.

order_book.quote: Our DevCo shows a strong market acceptance, reflected in 900 megawatts of orders already booked in H1 '27.

product_mix.quote: Our RE portfolio loan book stands at close to INR86,000 crores, which is 27% increase over last year.

other.statement: Net credit-impaired assets down 50% to 0.11% as of Sep 2026

margin.quote: EBITDA came in at Rs. 69.14 crores versus Rs. 44.68 crores last year, growth of 54.8% with EBITDA margin of 7.4%.

margin.quote: Second half, typically is slightly better for us seasonally because there are obviously slightly higher sales and also operating leverage kicks in. capex.statement: FY27 capex of ~Rs 400 crore on track and largely completed
capex.quote: CAPEX for this year, which we have guided for around Rs. 400 crores, is on track, and largely the CAPEX has been done, as Pramodji said in his call comments earlier.

risk.quote: Yes, B.V.K. will answer the question regarding view. B.V.K. Reddy: Yes, see this is front-loaded already in the second quarter. So this is unusual. other.statement: Orgafeed revenue up 40% YoY in Q2 FY27; margins impacted by raw material costs not fully passed to farmers; exploring Maharashtra feed expansion after integrated facility operational
other.quote: Speaking about our Orgafeed business, it is continuing to deliver a strong growth with revenue increasing by 40% year-on-year in Q2 FY '27. However, margins were impacted by higher raw material costs, which could not be fully passed on to the farmers.

other.quote: No, it will go ahead. From March, we'll be -- March to April, we'll start our -- the liquid milk operations will start. And by September, we will -- September we'll start our powder operations.

guidance.statement: Q3 expected to be best ever quarter in almost all businesses with strong growth over Q2
guidance.quote: We also believe that the EBITDA of the group has grown 20% from Q2 over Q1. We believe we will have similar growth rates of EBITDA sequentially from Q2 to Q3. Q3 this year is likely to be our best ever quarter in almost all our businesses.

guidance.statement: OLX growth rates expected to surpass current 26% and cross 30-35% in coming quarters
guidance.quote: We feel the OLX growth rates, which you see, will be surpassed in the coming quarters. We of course think the growth rate will cross 30%, 35% in the coming quarters at OLX.

margin.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded to 36% in Q2 from 33% YoY and 31% QoQ
margin.quote: EBITDA margins come out at 36%. As you know, your company is focused on building a best-in-class margin structure. You can see here, EBITDA margin has jumped from 33% last year quarter to 36% and 36% over 31% previous quarter same time.

margin.statement: Consumer group EBITDA margin reached 41% in Q2
margin.quote: If you look at the consumer group, which is the next slide, revenue from operations are up 4%, EBITDA is up 5%, and margins have come to 41%, and PAT is up 13%.

margin.statement: OLX EBITDA margin improved to 32%
margin.quote: OLX is actually, revenues had a very strong growth. We had 28% half yearly growth, a 26% quarter growth. EBITDA margins are up to 32% in OLX, and EBITDA growth is up to 36% here.

order_book.statement: SAMIL auctioned 2.35 lakh vehicles out of 1.56 million listed (annualized for Q2)
order_book.quote: We have about 1.56 million vehicles which were listed, of which 2.35 lakh were auctioned. These are annualized for Q2.

capex.statement: No significant CAPEX or working capital expense; most profits convert to cash
capex.quote: The good thing in a company like ours is there is no CAPEX really. There is no really working capital expense, and most of the profits we generate, almost all the profits we generate go to cash.

capex.statement: VAYA Live development cost not material as built on proprietary data and AI code without LLM token costs
capex.quote: The costs are not significant, and I will tell you why. Because a lot of V AYA is built, first of all, it is built on AI code. The second part is that it is built on proprietary data. We do not buy data or use LLM data

product_mix.statement: New products like Elite Buyer, Elite Seller, VAYA Live driving growth; existing products also contributing strongly
product_mix.quote: The growth rates you are seeing are 26%, and the growth rates are going to increase over the next quarter and the quarter after that, is a large part due to the existing products and not just new products. I think new products will come on top of that.

product_mix.statement: OEM revenue share in consumer business at ~74%, up slightly from ~70% previously
product_mix.quote: About 74% would be OEM in total revenues.

risk.statement: Base effect from GST reduction in Sep 2025 inflated Q2 FY26 growth to 37%, creating tough YoY comparison
risk.quote: The one big event last year, in fact, it has been game changing and great credit to the government in the entire automotive industry. I think anybody in automotive has seen a massive jump last year. There is a base effect there.

other.statement: Monthly active users (MAU) at 76 million average for Q2; organic traffic at 96%
other.quote: We receive 76 million MAUs average for this quarter. Organic traffic has jumped to 96%.

other.statement: Adjusted EBITDA crossed INR 106 crores for the quarter; PAT at INR 66 crores
other.quote: Adjusted EBITDA, which is a cash proxy, has crossed INR 106 crores for the quarter. PAT is at INR 66 crores and as I told you earlier, our cash balances are at INR 1,400 crores as of 30th September.

guidance.statement: Total insurance premium expected over ₹40,000 Cr for FY27
guidance.quote: The total insurance premium for the quarter was ₹9,385 Cr, up 38% year-on-year, setting us up well for over ₹40,000 Cr this year.

demand.statement: GST reduction drove 18% industry growth for 6 months; price elasticity ~1; growth normalized by March; Q4 YoY may not show growth
demand.quote: There was an 18% reduction of GST, and that was passed on to the customer. This is a very important data point for informing everyone. For the first 6 months, we saw an incremental 18% growth in the industry.

demand.statement: Demand has been tough this year requiring higher marketing spend to generate leads
demand.quote: Actually, demand has been very tough, and I think we've had to spend a lot more money. So I would say that if you look at it on a two-year basis, you'll find it's not that dramatic.

margin.statement: PAT margin improved from 8% to 9% in Q2 FY27
margin.quote: PAT grew 43% to ₹192 Cr, and PAT margin improved from 8% to 9%.

order_book.statement: Core renewal and trail revenue over ₹1,000 Cr on rolling 12-month basis, up 42% YoY
order_book.quote: And our core renewal and trail revenue is now over ₹1,000 Cr, it's almost ₹1,100 Cr. On a rolling 12-month basis, up 42% year-on-year.

order_book.statement: PB Partners revenue about ₹700 Cr for the quarter
order_book.quote: PB Partners revenue; it's about ₹700 Cr.

capex.statement: PB Health on track for ₹40-45 Cr monthly run rate by March (~₹500 Cr annual), breaking even
capex.quote: We are on track of executing a few new hospitals. So, around March, we should have a run rate somewhere between ₹40-45 Cr per month, which is about ₹500 Cr for the year.

capex.statement: CapEx increased substantially to support office expansion and staff growth
capex.quote: As we have spoken earlier about this, that we have been building capacity, we have been ramping up, and P0 remains our growth. So, this CapEx is largely towards supporting the expansion of offices, as well as supporting the staff.

pricing_cost.statement: Health customers pay on average 9% less and up to 30% less than some other channels
pricing_cost.quote: On price reduction, for the plans they choose, our health customers pay, on average, 9% less and up to 30% less than some other channels.

product_mix.statement: Paisabazaar adding suppliers, new business lines (bill payments, wealth - bonds, FDs); disbursals flat QoQ due to focus on distribution over marketing
product_mix.quote: We saw an opportunity in our customer strata, and we saw a lot of partnerships or suppliers that we could add on our platform, and that will help us grow disbursal. So, in fact, we see in our deck, we've mentioned a few banks that we've onboarded.

product_mix.statement: Core online new health and term grew 42% YoY, new health grew 46% YoY
product_mix.quote: Core online new health and term grew 42% YoY, and within this, new health gr ew 46% YoY

fund_raise.statement: No cash burn intent; cash position is capability but NPV more critical; will assess after final regulations
fund_raise.quote: Mentally, the intent is not a cash burn intent. Now, let's see when the paper comes out, and what opportunities arise out of it, and what situations arise out of it.

risk.statement: POSP business model under question due to open architecture payout structure; may need transition time
risk.quote: The way the current regulations are, it says, if you are open architecture, you're going to get paid less than the closed architecture. That in my opinion, does not leave scope for POSP the way it is today.

other.statement: Health claims settlement ratio 97% vs industry 87%; 11,156 rejected claims worth ₹185 Cr reopened and paid last year
other.quote: On claims in the health insurance industry, the industry data says 87% of health claims are settled. That same number for Policybazaar customers is 97%. Last year, 11,156 rejected claims worth ₹185 Cr were reopened after initial rejection and paid.

other.statement: Mis-selling complaints: 16 per 10,000 customers in life vs benchmark 30-53; 21 claim complaints per 10,000 claims in health vs benchmark 29-54
other.quote: On mis-selling, in the life insurance category, we get 16 complaints from our customers per 10,000 customers. This is against a benchmark of 30 to 53. In health insurance, we get 21 claim complaints for every 10,000 claims. This is against a benchmark of 29 to 54.

guidance.statement: Management targets positive SSSG for full FY27
guidance.quote: Our focus remains on delivering positive SSSG for FY '27 as a whole and the festive quarter will be an important one of that journey.

guidance.statement: Aim to nearly double square footage over next 5 years with calibrated expansion across Tier-1, Tier-2, Tier-3 cities
guidance.quote: Over the next 5 years, we aim to significantly expand our footprint with the potential to nearly double our square feet in terms of size.

guidance.statement: Q3 FY27 expected to deliver good numbers; confident of positive SSSG for full FY27
guidance.quote: Certainly, yes, Ankit. Q3 should deliver a good number for us.

guidance.statement: Target 25-30 dailywear stores by end of FY27; currently 21 operational vs 15 in Q1
guidance.quote: We remain committed to our target of 25-30 daily stores by the end of FY '27.

margin.statement: Exceptional expense Rs 3.4 cr in Q2, Rs 9.9 cr in H1 FY27 from store closure capex write-offs (one-off)
margin.quote: During the quarter, we recognized an exceptional expense of Rs. 3.4 crores taking the total of our H1 FY '27 to Rs. 9.9 crores. This exceptional expenditure is a write-off of capital expenditure on account of store closures which has happened through the 6 months. It is a direct consequence of our network consolidation strategy and it is a one-off item.

margin.statement: Estimate Q3 FY27 gross margin impact of 100-200 bps from RM inflation; Q2 impact was ~200 bps
margin.quote: My estimate is, this quarter, we had 200 basis points impact on our GM. I think the next Q3, we should be having a gross margin impact of anywhere between 100 and 200 bps is my estimate.

margin.statement: Q2 FY27 gross margin 60.8%, down ~200 bps due to higher fabric costs from geopolitical situation; intend to pass on RM inflation via calibrated pricing
margin.quote: Gross margins for the quarter stood at 60.8%. As I mentioned on the last call, fabric prices have gone up due to the geopolitical situation, and this higher-cost inventory has started flowing in Quarter 2. We intend to pass on the raw material inflation through calibrated pricing actions which will help restore gross margins in the coming quarters.

capex.statement: COCO model preferred over FOCO for full inventory control; operating cash flow expected to exceed store opening investments
capex.quote: For our kind of supply chain, for our kind of template, we feel COCO is better. And because our payback periods have been attractive, even if we are going to be investing and doubling our square feet, from a cash flow perspective, our operating cash flow will be far higher than what we are going to be investing on store openings.

pricing_cost.statement: Fabric/yarn cost inflation running at 8-10% blended; RM prices cooled slightly in Jul-Aug but remain high
pricing_cost.quote: It is between 8% and 10% is what I understand. Because see, the yarn prices and fabric prices have changed every month. But if I have to just take a blended, I think it is about 8%-10% is what we see.

pricing_cost.statement: Price hikes initiated on certain articles recently; more planned post-festive; expect gross margin impact to stabilize in next 2 quarters
pricing_cost.quote: We have done price hike for certain articles, we have just recently done. And we are in the midst of doing price hike for some other articles as well. So, I think the offset against the gross margin will take a couple of quarters. But I think it will stabilize in the next 2 quarters.

product_mix.statement: Value-added non-leggings portfolio contributes 70% of revenue, reflecting steady premiumization
product_mix.quote: Our value-added non-leggings portfolio now contributes to 70% of the revenue reflecting the steady premiumization of what Go Colors offers.

product_mix.statement: Dailywear concept stores (21) achieving ~Rs 1,000 sales per sq ft per month; topwear and menswear (10-12% space) contributing in these larger format stores
product_mix.quote: Like I mentioned in my previous calls, we continue to deliver about Rs. 1,000 of sales per square feet per month, which is a good number for us, which we think to begin with.

other.statement: Opened 9 new stores and closed 23 smaller format stores in Q2 FY27; H1 FY27: 24 openings, 89 closures; total 737 EBOs across 196 cities as of Sep 2026

other.quote: Working capital days stood at 134 days, with inventory days improving to 94 days from 100 days at the end of Q1, now within the 90-100 day range which we had guided earlier this year.

capex.statement: New projects target at least 15% IRR and 7-year payback; includes replacement capex, owned trains, fleet electrification
capex.quote: But any new project that we're doing, we're targeting like it's at least a 15% IRR and a 7-year payback, if that kind of helps the guidance a little bit.

capex.statement: Indore ICD civil and rail works started; targeting operational by December 2027 with volume ramp-up over 2 years
capex.quote: Yes, it's in full swing. So civil and rail works have started. We're targeting by within December 2027, if we can be operational. And following, say, 6 months after that, it can start contributing some good volumes. It takes 2 years to ramp it up after operations, but we should start seeing something within the first year itself.

pricing_cost.statement: Price increases passed through after fuel hikes; Ankleshwar EXIM mix lowers realization per TEU due to shorter lead distance
pricing_cost.quote: There was some price increases. This was mainly after fuel hikes came in, so we've passed that on to customers. But our cost also increased accordingly to that. So that was pretty much a pass-through. Ankleshwar mix, yes, that has also made some difference. And with EXIM coming in Gateway Distriparks Limited and at Ankleshwar, you'll see the realization per TEU go down a little bit because of its

pricing_cost.statement: Indian Railways double-stack discount on upper stack given to CTOs; not passed separately to customers, based on overall volumes
pricing_cost.quote: In fact, once you're saying that there's a discount on the upper stack. So that is given by Indian Railways to the CTO. But again, it depends that how much double stack you are able to do that.

product_mix.statement: New Snowman capacity all cold temperature-controlled with minimal dry share; existing dry capacity 10-12%
product_mix.quote: So, the new facilities are all cold temperature controlled. We have a very minimal share of dry there. Typically, we're planning to shut a chamber and do it in initial time and then convert everything into frozen.

other.quote: No, we typically take like 6% to 8% increase, which is expected in the coming year. When we do a contract, we take that -- we consider that sort of an increase already in the pricing.

other.statement: Snowman 5PL not aggressive due to low margins; one customer negative growth offset by another; targeting profitable accounts only
other.quote: So so far, we have not added any new customer in this financial year in 5PL. A few of the discussions are on the verge of closure, yet not concluded. In terms of growth within the partners who are already there, one of the customer has shown a negative growth, but rest have shown a positive growth. And overall segment grew by 1% or 2% to be precise.

guidance.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 is approximately Rs 200 crore, in line with previous year; FY28 capex not quantified as customer schedules not finalized
guidance.quote: For this year, we have already laid out the guidance that largely in line with what we had in the previous year of Rs. 200 crores approximately.

demand.statement: Passenger vehicle industry volumes grew 25% YoY and 14% QoQ; company grew ahead of industry driven by premiumization, new model launches across EV and ICE, and Greenfield contributions
demand.quote: The passenger vehicle industry continued to witness healthy growth with volumes increasing 25% year -on-year and 14% sequentially. We grew ahead of the industry reflecting the continued trust of our customers and our ability to capture growth opportunities.

demand.statement: Second half will be compared against higher base post GST reduction; industry expected to continue healthy growth; festive period expected to deliver strong revenue growth
demand.quote: Based on current visibility, we expect the industry to continue registering healthy growth. The combination of healthy industry growth, continued premiumization, driving higher content per new vehicle and new model launches provide a favorable backdrop for us.

margin.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 9.2% from 7.6% in Q1 through operational efficiencies; headwinds from copper prices (+6% QoQ, +54% YoY), minimum wage revisions, and inflation persist
margin.quote: EBITDA margins stood at 9.2% improving from 7.6% in Q1 through continued focus on operational efficiencies which led to a resilient performance while headwinds from higher copper prices, minimum wage revisions and other inflationary pressures remain.

capex.statement: FY28 capex depends on customer schedules not yet finalized; clarity will come when plans are laid down
capex.quote: FY28, it all depends on because we are supplying to our customers. So, right now, the schedules have not finalized where we are setting in. So, in terms of giving you the indication in terms of the capitalization at this moment for FY '28 would be very difficult.

pricing_cost.statement: Copper is a pass-through item with typical 3-month lag for majority of customers; continuously engaging with customers to recover incremental costs
pricing_cost.quote: As we have highlighted previously, copper is a pass-through item with a typical time lag of about three months for recovery from majority of the customers. We are continuously engaging in constructive discussions with our customers to recover these increment costs.

pricing_cost.statement: Copper price recovery lag is mostly one quarter, up to six months in some cases; if copper stabilizes, buy and sell at same price within one to three quarters
pricing_cost.quote: So, basically, as the team has informed that we have a lag of mostly quarter. In some cases, smaller cases would have been up to 6 months, but mostly, the majority is 3 months. So, that's the lag. So, if the copper price is stabilized and on a quarter-on-quarter basis, it's there, but it has not stabilized, then we can't predict this now. But, to answer your question, and in one quarter, two quart

product_mix.statement: EVs accounted for 10% of revenue in Q2 and 9.3% in H1; premiumization driving higher content per vehicle across EV and ICE platforms
product_mix.quote: EVs accounted for 10% of our revenue during the quarter and 9.3% for the first half of the year.

product_mix.statement: Zonal architecture transition discussed for 20 years; content per vehicle increasing due to customer aspirations and innovations beyond just transportation; not solely dependent on architecture
product_mix.quote: So, far, we have seen that there has been a content increase there have been discussions on the, because the aspirations of the people, and also the innovations of the carmakers to not just let it be a car, but it's more than just a mode of transportation that has led to content increase.

risk.statement: Second half growth percentages may not be as wide as last year due to higher base post GST cut; copper price volatility and wage inflation remain headwinds
risk.quote: But the range of growth in terms of percentages may not be as wide as what was with respect to last year.

other.statement: Company expands capacity when utilization hits around 80%; expanded facilities in past 2-3 years to stay ahead of customer growth
other.quote: The moment it hits around 80%, we are in an expansion mode. And you would see that as the customers keep growing and the customers are putting up new facilities, the company will set up and expand its facilities.

other.statement: Revenue grew 47% YoY and 19% QoQ; EBITDA grew 34% YoY and 45% QoQ; PAT grew 35% YoY and 54% QoQ
other.value: Revenue 47% YoY, 19% QoQ; EBITDA 34% YoY, 45% QoQ; PAT 35% YoY, 54% QoQ
other.quote: We are pleased to report a strong performance this quarter with the revenue growing 47% year-on-year and 19% sequentially. EBITDA increased 34% year -on-year and 45% sequentially while profit after tax registered growth of 35% and 54% respectively.

guidance.quote: you are right that the margins will be more than the 30%, which we are always guiding, but we are being conservative and taking into consideration the various factors which might affect the war situations come up or the pricing effects, which can come up. order_book.statement: Line of sight on 14 of 16 Magnum production blocks: 2 for LSM, 12 for CEM contracts expected to commercialize over 2-3 years
order_book.quote: We now do have line of sight on 14 of the 16 production blocks at Magnum. 2 are earmarked for LSM products, the remaining 12 are earmarked for CEM contracts, which we expect to commercialize over the next 2 to 3 years.

capex.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR350-370 crores, lower than prior estimate as major civil work at Magnum is complete and equipment orders will be timed to production start
capex.quote: INR350 crores is kept, and I think so we'll be around INR350 crores and maybe INR370 crores, not more than that because you understand if you see the picture, lots of the civil work is done on the 4 blocks, we are already ready and other 4 blocks also. So major chunk is already done.

capex.statement: Baker Hughes new products covered by original Strata site capex; no additional capex required
capex.quote: This will all be covered by original capex from the Strata site.

capex.statement: CWIP of INR700 crores largely for Site 5 (Magnum); ~INR400 crores expected to be capitalized by end of FY27
capex.quote: It's a Site 5 majorly. And by end of this year, this financial year, we expect that approximately INR400 crores should be capitalized.

pricing_cost.statement: CEM contracts have price pass-through for raw material cost increases; strategic raw material inventory built for Milliken project (US imports with lead time)
pricing_cost.quote: And of course, it's a contract manufacturing. So any price increase tomorrow will be passed through, of course. So this is the case. And once the production is full-fledged going on and the sales are happening, the inventory levels will come to a considerable lower level as we have always spoken about the CEM.

risk.statement: Management avoids hazardous chemistries (HF, F2, H2S) and focuses on safety-compatible competencies; says no to inquiries quickly to maintain strategic focus
risk.quote: There are certain chemistries and technologies that we will not take up. For example, HF, F2, H2S. These are chemistries that we will not take up. We have our own hazards that we work with. We want -- we will be -- we are very practical in terms of the approach from the safety perspective in terms of the competencies that we take up.

other.statement: Working capital cycle at ~165 days (up 3 days from March) due to inventory build-up at new sites; management expects quarter-on-quarter improvement
other.quote: The working capital cycles will be improving. Currently also, it is around 165 days, which is 3 days higher than the 31st March, mainly because of the inventories which have been swelled up because of the new sites which have come up. But we are mindful of that, and things will be improving quarter-on-quarter for sure.

other.statement: LSM pipeline: 12-15 projects in R&D; target minimum 2 LSM product launches per year
other.quote: Approximately 15 projects -- 12 to 15 projects on LSM side are going on in the R&D. And we plan to launch subject to our plan not being moving towards the CEM side is 2 products on LSM side every year minimum.

guidance.statement: Target 40-50% revenue growth for CDMO/CMO segment in FY27
guidance.quote: We remain on track to achieve our target of 40% to 50% revenue growth over last year on this business segment.

guidance.statement: Xanthine revenue expected to reach INR1,400-1,500 crores at full capacity if prices remain high
guidance.quote: Yes, if the prices remain high, we expect this to go up to INR1,400 crores to INR1,500 crores.

guidance.statement: CDMO long-term target of INR1,000 crores revenue maintained
guidance.quote: See, as I mentioned, our target remains 100 million or INR1,000 crores, whichever comes first.

guidance.statement: API segment expected to grow 10-15% annually over next 3-4 years
guidance.quote: we'll have 10% to 15% growth every year on this business, or we probably in certain years we can have higher growth also.

demand.statement: API growth in Q2 largely volume-driven after steroid debottlenecking; headwinds subsiding
demand.quote: This is largely volume-driven. The current growth was largely volume-driven.

margin.quote: The EBITDA margins have remained healthy at 22.2% as compared to 17.7% in the same quarter last year.

margin.statement: CDMO growth and raw material pass-through to drive absolute gross margin increase in H2
margin.quote: But in the absolute number, I think gross margins will keep on increasing whatever as we do more quality business going forward.

order_book.statement: CDMO has 59 active projects (39 commercial, 20 development) across 23 customers
order_book.quote: The number of active projects now is 59, out of which 39 projects are in commercial stages and 20 are under different stages of development, both at customers end.

capex.statement: Total capex targeted at INR350-400 crores for FY27
capex.quote: Overall, we have targeted a capex of around -- total capex of around INR350 crores to INR400 crores for the year.

pricing_cost.statement: Xanthine realization up 10-15% YoY on average; spot segment prices under pressure but pharma/beverage stable
pricing_cost.quote: The xanthine prices, on an average, our realization is up, 10% to 15% over last year, realization.

pricing_cost.statement: Passing on elevated raw material costs to customers in Xanthine and API segments
pricing_cost.quote: Due to geopolitical turmoil, the raw material costs have stayed elevated and we are passing on the raw material increase to our customers.

product_mix.statement: API mix shifting toward regulated markets (57% regulated, 33% ROW, 10% non-regulated)
product_mix.quote: The sub-segment wise breakup is 57% for the regulated market, 33% for the ROW market and 10% for the non -regulated market.

risk.statement: Xanthine spot segment pricing under pressure; pharma and beverage segments more stable
risk.quote: In Xanthine, there are three segments. So, in the spot segment, the prices will have pressure. I think the pharma and the beverages section, anyway, we will have more stability on the price.

other.statement: Atali new blocks expected to achieve 1.2-1.4x asset turns
other.quote: But I think the newer blocks, we have given the guidance that it will have 1.2 to 1.4 kind of a turn on asset side.

other.statement: Xanthine expanded capacity to reach full production by end of FY27, full utilization over next two years
other.quote: The ramp-up of xanthine expanded capacity is progressing and we plan to achieve the full capacity by the end of FY27 and we will achieve the utilization sequentially in the next year.

guidance.statement: Management guided for FY28 consolidated revenue of ₹2,500 crore with 14% EBITDA and 11% PAT, but said new guidance with higher margins will be announced very soon.
guidance.quote: As I have been suggesting, we are looking towards FY28 with CCL, on the old numbers given in the past guidance, including consolidated, at a ₹2,500 crore top line, with EBITDA of 14% and PAT of 11%.

guidance.statement: Management expects FY27 PAT margin around 6.25% and tax rate near last year's ~15%.
guidance.quote: The PAT margin this year is expected to be around 6.25%.

guidance.statement: Management targets base business revenue of ₹1,315 crore in FY27 and ₹1,800 crore by FY28.
guidance.quote: Last year we did ₹1,080 crores. This year we are reaching the projected target of ₹1,315 crores and we are very much in line with this year's proj ections. Up to FY28, we are targeting to reach ₹1,800 crores as top line

demand.statement: PCB manufacturers fully booked for 2-4 years, entering long-term contracts; CCL shortage structural; demand not a constraint for Ratnaveer.
demand.quote: All the PCB players are fully booked for the next two, three, four years, and they are also entering into long-term contracts, so the demand for CCL will regularly feed all the PCB manufacturers.

margin.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 10.82% (₹42.13 cr), PAT margin 6.22% (₹24.07 cr); gross margin dipped to 9.44% from 10.33% due to new product expenses booked before sales.
margin.quote: The gross margin was 10.33% in Quarter 1 and 9.44% in Quarter 2. It has dropped marginally, and the only reason is that the new products are on the way and the expenses have been booked while the sales are yet to come, so the gross margin has dipped slightly.

order_book.statement: Single CCL line has potential for ₹500 crore revenue; orders of required size and quantum already secured to support that revenue potential.
order_book.quote: A single line of business has the potential to generate ₹500 crore in revenue, and the company has already secured orders of the required size and quantum to support this revenue potential.

capex.statement: Phase 2 capex of ~₹58 crore ongoing for fasteners, tubes, sheet metal and clips to support revenue growth to ₹1,800 crore.
capex.quote: Yes, our CapEx for Phase 2, for fasteners, tubes and pipes, and also for sheet metal components and clips, is already ongoing. This year we are also spending CapEx of around ₹58 crores, which was already planned last year, and this will help us reach from a ₹1,400 crore top line to ₹1,800 crores.

capex.statement: CCL project planned investment of ₹338 crore over 2-3 years plus ₹86 crore for captive solar plant, approved under ECMS scheme.
capex.quote: The planned investment by Ratnaveer is ₹338 crores over the next two to three years, approved under the ECMS scheme by the Government of Gujarat as well as the Government of India. The plan also covers an ₹86 crore investment in a solar plant for captive use.

pricing_cost.statement: CCL pricing at par or 0.5-1% below Chinese imports; customers gain on wait time, logistics, forex risk and faster delivery.
pricing_cost.quote: At this moment, for the initial bookings, we can keep the pricing at par with the Chinese, or slightly 0.5% to 1% lower than the Chinese, and customers get extra advantages: on wait time, on logistics cost, on foreign exchange fluctuation risk, and they can also get deliveries quicker and faster.

product_mix.statement: CCL facility will produce Tg 140-180, FR4, prepreg, single/double-sided, copper thickness 15-35 microns, thickness range 0.8-3.2 mm covering automotive, EV, drone, satellite, aerospace, data centres.
product_mix.quote: we are producing from 140 Tg to 180 Tg, and we are concentrating on all PCB manufacturing companies, including the automotive industry, EVs, electrical and electronic vehicles, the drone industry, satellite equipment, aerospace and all kinds of electronic devices that use CCL.

fund_raise.statement: No plan for any equity raise or new fundraise; rights issue completed successfully.
fund_raise.quote: No, not at all. There is no plan right now for any kind of equity raise or any new fundraise.

risk.statement: Initial teething challenges may cause 2-3 week delays in machine synchronisation and formulation establishment; technical team confident on roadmap.
risk.quote: Initially, testiing challenges are possible, maximum two to three weeks here or there, but the product can be established

other.statement: CCL raw material prices increased 40-50% max vs 300%+ finished goods price increase; no domestic CCL producers currently.
other.quote: Raw material prices have also increased, but not equally to 300%; it can be an increase of 40% to 50% at maximum.

other.statement: No anti-dumping duty on CCL as no domestic producers exist; ECMS and PLI schemes support equipment imports and engineer visas from China.
other.quote: There is no producer available in our country right now, so there is no scope for any kind of anti-dumping duty.

guidance.statement: Wire and cable EBIT margin target 9.5% for FY27 and ~10.5% for FY28
guidance.quote: As per those, we have targeted to achieve growth of 9.5% EBIT margins in our wire and cable segment, where even if you see on a half yearly basis, we are at 9.6%. So our margin guidance remains the same. To be specific, 9.5% for this year and approx. 10.5% for FY 2028.

guidance.statement: FMEG segment targeting full-year EBIT breakeven in FY27
guidance.quote: Our objective remains to achieve full year breakeven at segment profit level in FY '27.

guidance.statement: Full-year volume growth guidance revised to 14-15% for FY27
guidance.quote: Earlier, we were expecting around 16%-18%, and we have just fine-tuned around 15% and looking to the various factors, what we have seen volatility also in terms of so many factors which impact.

demand.statement: Wire volumes grew double-digit, cable volumes single-digit in Q2; exports grew faster than domestic
demand.quote: Our overall volume growth was in high single -digits, where wire outpacing cables. If we further see, our wires were growing in double digits, while cables, we have seen a single digit growth. And same in our exports. Exports growth was faster than domestic.

demand.statement: H2 typically sees higher volumes year-on-year; confident of achieving full-year growth plan
demand.quote: If you see normally H2 is always we have seen higher volumes year-on-year. I have experienced in over my experience of previous so many years. Still I think we will be able to achieve this, our growth plan, whatever we have done, even based on these higher volumes. We are quite confident to achieve that.

margin.statement: H1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 130 bps to 8.9%
margin.quote: Operating EBITDA grew by 79% of approximately INR 571 crores, compared with INR 319 crores last year. EBITDA margins expanded by around 130 basis points to 8.9% from 7.6%.

margin.statement: Wire and cable segment margin improved to 9.6% in H1 FY27 from 8.4%
margin.quote: For H1, wire and cable revenue stood at approximately INR 5,890 crores, growing 55% year-on-year. Segment profit grew by 78% to around INR 568 crores, with segment margin expanding to 9.6% from 8.4% last year.

margin.statement: FMEG H1 loss margin narrowed to 2.2% from 4.5%
margin.quote: For H1, the segment losses reduced to approximately INR 12 crores from approximately INR 19 crores last year. The H1 loss margins narrowed to 2.2% from 4.5%, supported by growth in scale and improved absorption of operating costs.

capex.statement: FY27 capex plan of INR 550-600 crores on track, excluding UM Cables and Rajasthan land
capex.quote: Secondly, yes, of course, whatever we have planned in the beginning of the year in the range of like INR 550 crores to INR 600 crores, it will be there. As our capex plan is on track and we are executing on time.

capex.statement: INR 200 crores approved for land acquisition in Rajasthan for future expansion
capex.quote: Further, the board has approved an investment of INR 200 crores towards land acquisition in Rajasthan to support our future expansion plan.

capex.statement: Next year capex estimated around INR 300 crores
capex.quote: Seems okay. There may be some plus minus, but as of now it seems okay, INR 300 crores.

pricing_cost.statement: Gross margin contraction due to product mix and high raw material base prices
pricing_cost.quote: One is, of course, product mix is there. Secondly, since we are working on very high raw material base prices, there will be some impact. If we see overall profitability, as per our business plan only, we are moving ahead.

risk.statement: Volatility in commodity prices and near-term demand fluctuations acknowledged
risk.quote: We remain attentive to commodity price movements and their impact on both realization and margins. Overall, we are encouraged by our H1 performance while recognizing the importance of sustainable volumes, cash conversion, and discipline execution in the quarters ahead.

other.statement: Signed business transfer agreement to acquire UM Cables for ~INR 77 crores
other.quote: On 25th September 2026, we entered into new business transfer agreement with UM Cables Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of Usha Martin Limited. For the proposed acquisition of UM Cables business undertaking engaged in manufacturing and selling optical fibre and related cables. The agreed consideration is approximately INR 77 crores, subject to post-closing adjustments.

other.statement: Net working capital cycle improved to 46 days in Sep'26 from 49 days in Mar'26
other.quote: Our net working capital cycle improved to 46 days as of September '26, from 49 days in March and 50 days in June.

guidance.statement: FY27 ROA guidance raised to 2% for full year from earlier quarterly target
guidance.quote: We have given the guidance of ROA 2%, quarterly ROA by the year end. But as things stand today, our guidance changes to ROA of 2% for the full year.

guidance.statement: FY27 cost-to-income ratio guidance maintained at around 60%
guidance.quote: We aim to maintain cost-to-income ratio of around 60% for the year.

guidance.statement: FY27 credit cost expected around 2% for full year
guidance.quote: We estimate the same to remain in the range of 2% for the full year.

guidance.statement: FY28 credit cost estimated at 1.5%
guidance.quote: Next year, again, all the backlogs have already been cleared. We hope that 1.5% will be a good guess.

margin.statement: Q2 FY27 NIM at 8.2%; funding cost expected to marginally increase in Q3 but absorbable
margin.quote: Yield on advances continue to be in a comfortable zone and cost of funds remained largely stable in Q2 FY27, leading to net interest margin at 8.2%. The funding cost is expected to marginally go up in Q3 but have enough cushion to absorb in the current NIM levels.

order_book.statement: Total business Rs 52,400 crore, up 25% YoY; gross advances Rs 23,934 crore, up 25% YoY; deposits Rs 28,466 crore, up 24% YoY
order_book.quote: As of September 30, 2026, our total business stood at Rs. 52,400 crores, registering a healthy year-on-year growth of 25% compared to Rs. 42,031 crores of last year. During the same period, gross advance grew by 25%, while deposits increased by 24%, reflecting balanced growth across both sides of the balance sheet.

risk.statement: Vigilant on global tensions, RBI monetary stance, supply chain disruptions, weather-related issues
risk.quote: However, we remain vigilant on the global tensions, revised monetary stance by RBI, supply chain disruptions amid geopolitical tensions, and the recent weather-related issues.

other.statement: CASA ratio at 23.3%, grew 10% YoY slower than term deposits; targeting improvement via NTB, NR, TASC relationships by year-end
other.quote: CASA deposits grew at a slower pace than term deposits to Rs. 6,645 crores in Q2 FY27, registering a 10% Y-o-Y growth, with the CASA ratio standing at 23.3%. We are formulating various measures for prioritizing quality CASA acquisitions and focusing more on NTB, NR, and TASC relationships to achieve the targeted CASA level by end of the year.

other.statement: CARE ESG rating improved from 75.4 to 77.6; rated higher than industry in all three ESG aspects
other.quote: As a result, our CARE ESG rating has improved from 75.4 to 77.6. The Bank has been rated higher than the industry in all three aspects of environmental, social and governance, thus reflecting our continued progress towards responsible and sustainable growth.

guidance.statement: Management does not provide forward-looking volume or margin numbers but expects to outgrow the AC industry and improve margins via PLI discount rollback and mix shift
guidance.quote: Rabindra-ji, we don't give out forward-looking numbers. But yes, we are looking at industry to grow and even competitive terms. And as EPACK continues its focus on increasing its share of business and growing partnership with newer customers, we definitely believe that we should outgrow the industry.

demand.statement: Industry primary and secondary AC sales improved in Q2 with comfortable channel inventory, giving a clean start for the coming season
demand.quote: Primary sales for room air conditioners in July to September quarter were better than last year. Last year, wherein unseasonal rains, destocking around GST transition weighed down the industry, the quarter has been comparatively much better both in terms of primary and secondary sales.

margin.statement: Gross margin improved to 12.8% in Q2 FY27 from 12.4% YoY on a like-to-like basis excluding PLI income
margin.quote: So if we neglect the PLI, the gross margin last year was approximately 12.4%, which now is 12.8%. So on a like-to-like basis, the gross margins have improved, although there has been a lag in passing the commodity impact.

margin.statement: Margin improvement levers: rolling back PLI discounts passed to brands, and mix shift toward higher-margin SDA/LDA; no explicit margin guidance given
margin.quote: Again, in terms of the outlook for margin growth in the future, 2 areas which I mentioned earlier, one, with our discipline on recovering the PLI discounts, which are passed on to the brands earlier as we roll back in a phased manner, definitely, the margins would improve going forward. So that's one thing we see and we are working on. And two is the product mix. So with especially the large and s

margin.statement: Reported EBITDA margin 1.62% in Q2 FY27 vs 0.23% YoY; excluding PLI, underlying EBITDA improved ~INR14.6 cr YoY
margin.quote: EBITDA for the second quarter stood at INR7.1 crores compared to INR0.5 crores in quarter 2 financial year '26, representing an improvement of approximately INR6.6 crores. The EBITDA margin improved to 1.62% compared to 0.23% in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

order_book.statement: H1 FY27 revenue INR1,325 cr (+51.3% YoY); Q2 revenue INR439 cr (+106% YoY); non-RAC share 63% in Q2
order_book.quote: I'm pleased to share that EPACK Durable's delivered its highest ever first half revenue of INR1,325 crores in H1 of '27, up 51.3% year-on-year. In second quarter, revenue more than doubled to INR439 crores.

capex.statement: Capex plan INR470 cr announced 18 months ago; INR370 cr actualized by Sep 2026; balance INR100 cr staggered over next 6-12 months for washing machines and newer AC models
capex.quote: In terms of the overall capex, the announcement we made almost 18 months ago was that we are looking at a capex of close to INR470 crores, of which sale is INR370 crores is what has been actualized till end of September. So -- and with this mostly everything has been already put to use and the plants are largely done.

pricing_cost.statement: Forex loss of ~INR10 cr in H1 FY27 dragged reported margins; rupee depreciation vs USD/CNY cannot be passed on in real time
pricing_cost.quote: what Rajeshji said in his opening remarks, the company has booked a forex loss of approximately INR10 crores, which has also led to a reduction in the gross margin, what we see in the numbers.

pricing_cost.statement: RAC prices increased 15-20% YoY model-to-model due to commodity and forex; pass-through largely covers cost escalation but with a quarterly lag
pricing_cost.quote: In that sense, so the pricing overall compared to last year same quarter, the increase has been approximately 15% to 20% vary from model to model. So that's the approximate price increase, which has hap pened because of the commodity and the forex this

product_mix.statement: SDA and LDA grew 57% YoY in Q2 (62% in H1); washing machines and air fryers led growth; non-RAC now ~50% of revenue mix
product_mix.quote: Small domestic and large domestic appliances grew 57%. Washing machines and air fryers led the growth and non -RAC business contributed 63% of the revenue for this quarter. For half year, SDA and LDA grew 62%.

risk.statement: PLI scheme final year; budgeted INR5,000 cr largely unutilized; extension discussions ongoing with Ministry/DPIIT; PLI discounts being rolled back in phased manner to normalize margins
risk.quote: Shreyans, yes, this is the last year for the PLI for EPACK Durable. And for last year and this year, currently, we are not accruing any income in terms of the PLI. So based on our current discussion and the representation done to the Ministry and the DPIIT, the budgeted amount for the PLI for AC, which was roughly INR5,000 crores, which has largely remained unutilized with the governme nt. There i

other.statement: Compressor supply secured from Highly and GMCC; India now self-reliant in compressor capacity; no shortfall expected
other.quote: Yes. So in terms of Compressor, the current domestic manufacturing capability within India, which has now largely developed is we can claim that India is now self-reliant in terms of overall Compressor capacity available and the requirement. So we have tie-up in place. We have already been securing compressors from the 2 large players, Highly and GMCC, and they have ramped up their capacity.

other.statement: Customer base expanded to 72 across 19 categories; top-2 concentration down to 32% from 72% in FY26; new products launched (vacuum cleaners, tower fans, nutri blenders)
other.quote: We now serve 72 customers across 19 categories and top 2 customers in concentration has come down to 32% from 72% earlier in FY '26. During the year, we launched vacuum cleaners, tower fan, nutri blenders and added newer

guidance.statement: Targeting ICONiQ White volume of close to 14 million cases in FY27, implying over 25% year-on-year growth
guidance.quote: The plan for ICONiQ during the current year is to reach a level of close to 14 million cases, which is in excess of 25% growth by the year-end.

guidance.statement: Expecting topline growth in-line with stated guidance of mid-teens for FY27
guidance.quote: Overall, we expect the topline to grow in-line with the stated guidance of mid-teens.

guidance.statement: Targeting FY27 EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY26 despite supply chain disruptions
guidance.quote: We will continue to invest behind our core brands, super-premium to luxury portfolio and organisational capabilities, while maintaining FY27 EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY26.

guidance.statement: Expecting EBITDA margin benefit of approximately 300 basis points by FY28 and a further 150 basis points in FY29 from backward integration
guidance.quote: These initiatives are expected to improve supply security, drive structural cost efficienc ies, and support EBITDA margin expansion over the medium term, including an expected margin benefit of approximately 300 basis points by FY28 and a further 150 basis points in FY29

demand.statement: Q2 FY27 consolidated volumes crossed 10 million cases for first time, up 11.1% YoY; H1 FY27 saw record monthly sales on three occasions with highest-ever monthly volume of 3.5 million cases in September 2026
demand.quote: Q2FY27 marked an important milestone for ABD, with quarterly volumes crossing 10 million cases for the first time. Total volumes stood at 10 million cases, compared to 9.0 million cases in Q2FY26, representing growth of 11.1% year-on-year.

margin.statement: Q2 FY27 reported EBITDA margin at 12.4%, down 66 bps YoY; like-to-like EBITDA margin excluding supply chain impact would be 14.9%, up 186 bps YoY
margin.quote: Reported EBITDA stood at ₹143 crore, up 10.0% year-on-year and 19.2% quarter-on-quarter, with EBITDA margin at 12.4%. The margin was lower by 66 basis points year-on-year, reflecting our continued investments in core brands and the newly established super-premium to luxury portfolio.

order_book.statement: Announced first overseas local production arrangement for Officer's Choice Blue in Malaysia through asset-light co-bottling model in August 2026
order_book.quote: In August 2026, we announced our first overseas local production arrangement, for Officer's Choice Blue in Malaysia, through an asset-light co-bottling model with an established local partner.

order_book.statement: International footprint expanded to 42 countries in Q2 FY27 from 36 in Q4 FY26, targeting 50+ countries in next 12 months
order_book.quote: ABD has expanded its footprint to 42 countries in Q2FY27, compared to 36 countries in Q4FY26, with expansion in European and African markets and Australia during the year, reinforcing our position as one of India's leading spirits exporters by volume.

capex.statement: Total capex journey of approximately ₹1,600 crore, with 25% spent till FY26 and balance over next 3 years
capex.quote: We have embarked upon a journey of approximately ₹1,600 crores of capex. Till FY26, we have just spent 25% and over the next 3 years, we will spend the balance.

capex.statement: Annual maintenance capex estimated at ₹75-100 crore per annum excluding backward integration capex
capex.quote: Our annual maintenance capex would be in the region of ₹75 crores to ₹100 crores per annum.

risk.statement: Global supply chain disruptions from West Asia crisis estimated at ₹53 crore impact in H1 FY27 (₹29 crore in Q2); inflationary pressures and geopolitical developments being monitored
risk.quote: Global supply chain disruptions continued to have an impact during H1 FY27, with an estimated impact of ₹53 crore, but our underlying business fundamentals remain resilient and our medium-term margin levers remain intact.

other.statement: Commenced commercial operations at UP bottling facility with 6 million cases per annum capacity in October 2026
other.quote: In October 2026, we commenced commercial operations at our bottling facility, with an initial capacity of 6 million cases per annum.

other.statement: India Ratings upgraded ABD's rating by two notches to 'IND AA-' with Stable outlook; capex program to be funded through internal accruals and debt while maintaining leverage within defined framework
other.quote: We are also pleased that India Ratings & Research has upgraded ABD's rating by two notches to 'IND AA-' with a Stable outlook. We remain focused on disciplined capital deployment. Our capex program is planned to be funded through internal accruals and debt, while maintaining leverage within our defined framework through the investment cycle.

guidance.statement: FY27 closing targets: double-digit revenue growth, mid-high double-digit EBITDA growth, ~INR300 cr FCFF, PBT ~INR220-225 cr
guidance.quote: We think we are in for a good year, and we reiterate our position of double-digit growth here in top line, a mid-high double-digit growth in EBITDA, about INR300 crores of FCFF, and good PBT of at least double-digit higher than last year, close to INR220 crores, INR225 crores maybe.

guidance.statement: FY27 guidance: double-digit top-line growth, mid-double-digit EBITDA growth, INR300 cr+ net cash, double-digit PBT growth
guidance.quote: We expect a strong H2 FY27 performance and remain firmly on track to achieve our FY27 guida nce of double-digit top-line growth and mid-double-digit EBITDA growth with INR300 crores plus of net cash and a double-digit growth in PBT

margin.statement: Branded Apparel Q2 margin 8.8% (flat YoY); expect double-digit plus in 2 years; Q3 benefit from fresh stock at new prices, store closures, operating leverage
margin.quote: So, I think in a couple of years, we will be double digit plus. Improving every percentage point actually takes a lot of work. So, we should be double digit plus. That's the guidance right now.

margin.statement: High Value Cotton Shirting Q2 margin 9.5% (-200+ bps YoY); flax prices stabilising, newer orders at higher prices, plant cost cuts; expect double-digit plus EBITDA by year-end
margin.quote: And the margins in H2 would be much better than this because the cost-cutting measures are falling in place in the plants, and also the newer orders we have taken at higher prices. So those invoicing will happen in H2, so the margins would be better. And I believe that the EBITDA would be double-digit plus at the end of the year.

order_book.statement: Garmenting order book robust; factories booked till Jan-end/Feb 10-15; now booking for end-Feb; Europe inquiries up 30% H1 YoY, 50% Q2 YoY
order_book.quote: My factories are full till January end, maybe 10th-15th February. I'm booking for end February. And by next month, I'll be booking for March, so the year looks good.

pricing_cost.statement: Input costs elevated: Brent USD105-110/bbl, wool multi-year highs, cotton elevated, rupee 94-95/USD, freight high; B2B pass-through 50-60% of RM increase; fresh autumn-winter stock at new prices in Q3
pricing_cost.quote: Globally, persistent geopolitical tensions and ongoing shipping disruptions have kept Brent crude elevated in the range of USD105 to USD110 per barrel, sustaining input cost pressures across fibers, specialty dye chemicals are at high prices, and global freight tariffs remain high. At the same time, Indian rupee has traded near record lows, hovering between 94 and 95 against the US dollar, thereby

product_mix.statement: Premiumization driving mix: pure wool/poly-wool blends in Branded Textile; casual brands ColorPlus, Parx leading growth; smart casuals (polos, chinos, denims) with proprietary fabrics; linen strong in Shirting
product_mix.quote: Shifting fabric mix towards high-margin pure wool and linen, launching new premium products across our formal brands, Park Avenue and Raymond Ready-to-Wear, this accelerates our premiumization strategy. We are also expanding smart casuals: polos, chinos, denims, featuring proprietary fabric technologies like Air Shield, Flexfit, and Techno-Clean.

other.statement: Garmenting onboarding new global accounts from Europe; UK-India FTA traction; US-India tariff rationalization helping; EU FTA expected Dec signing to unlock further orders
other.quote: Growth was driven by robust order execution following the US-India tariff rationalization, early market traction from UK-India FTA, and onboarding new global accounts, especially from Europe.

other.statement: No explicit dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on net cash generation and debt-free balance sheet
other.quote: We maintained our fortified debt-free balance sheet, closing the quarter with a net cash surplus of INR69 crores as of September 2026.

guidance.statement: FY27 operating EBITDA guidance affirmed at Rs 7,000-7,700 crore
guidance.quote: We affirm our operating EBITDA guidance of Rs. 7,000 to Rs. 7,700 crores in FY '27.

guidance.statement: H2 FY27 expected to contribute 55-60% of full-year EBITDA guidance
guidance.quote: So, yes, Q4 shall be heavy, Q3 shall also be loaded. So, H2 overall shall be around 55 % to 60% of the overall EBITDA guidance is what we are looking at.

demand.statement: India solar demand annualized at 55-60 GW DC; rooftop+C&I ~15 GW, utility ~25 GW AC
demand.quote: All in all, around 60 gigawatts, 55 to 60 gigawatt demand is what is annually India doing.

margin.statement: US domestic manufacturing margin 8-9 cents/Wp (incl 7 cents IRA) vs India export margin 3-4 cents/Wp
margin.quote: While if you manufacture the same panel, let's say currently we are manufacturing the panels in the US, we are getting the operating margin of around 2 to 3 cents at utilization factor of 70% above, plus there is underlying 7 cents of EBITDA margin which adds up to it.

margin.statement: Q2 FY27 operating EBITDA margin 17.8% vs 18.2% Q1; underlying margin improved excluding US duty refund
margin.quote: Operating EBITDA was Rs. 1,335.2 crores while margin was 17.8%.

order_book.statement: Total order book Rs 59,200 crore as of Oct 26, 2026; module order book 25.6 GW
order_book.quote: Our total order book as on 26th of October '26, was around Rs. 59,200 crores. The module order book was 25.6 gigawatts.

order_book.statement: Export order book rationalized from 24% to 7.8% due to US Section 232; ~3 GW orders removed
order_book.quote: What have we exactly done is, Sweta, as you are aware, that Section 232 is enacted in US last quarter, owing to which there is a minimum import price in US for import of panels starting December 4.

capex.statement: Rs 30,000 crore capex program: 35% deployed, 28% under execution, 37% under planning
capex.quote: On our outlined capex program of approximately Rs. 30,000 crores, 35% is already deployed, 28% is under execution, and 37% is under planning stage.

capex.statement: Ingot/wafer 10 GW facility at Nagpur: civil 70% done; commercial production targeted September 2027; capex Rs 5,500 crore

capex.statement: Solar glass facility in Gujarat near Navsari: land acquired, technology discussions ongoing; target FY29 commissioning; Rs 3,900 crore planned

pricing_cost.statement: India DCR module spot: utility 19-20 cents, retail 22-23 cents; non-DCR: utility 12-12.5 cents, retail 13.5-14 cents

product_mix.statement: Retail revenue Rs 5,753 crore H1 FY27 (2x YoY), 37% of total; targeting Rs 10,000-11,000 crore full year
product_mix.quote: Our retail business revenues. It has reached Rs. 5,753 crores in H1 FY '27, almost 2x year-on-year, and accounted for 37% of total revenue for H1 FY '27.

product_mix.statement: Non-solar revenue share to rise from 15-20% to 30-35% in 2-3 years; long-term solar share 50-60%
product_mix.quote: Going ahead, it seems that with the higher growth in newer business verticals where we are investing around Rs. 30,000 crores, over 2.5 years, the contribution shall rise from 15 %-20% from these businesses to around 30% to 35% over next 2 to 3 years.

risk.statement: China technology transfer restrictions: no impact as all equipment orders secured for cell, battery, ingot/wafer
risk.quote: For China policy, as we have secured all our equipments in for cells as well as batteries, there is no impact. Ingot wafer also, the order and everything is being secured, so there is no impact.

other.statement: BESS: 5 GWh containerization facility commissioned last quarter; pack facility expected Q3 FY27; 3.5 GWh cell manufacturing pilot Q4 FY27
other.quote: In our BESS business, we are looking at commissioning 5 gigawatt -hour containerization * facility in Q3 FY '27 and 3.5 gigawatt-hour of battery cell manufacturing in this financial year.

other.statement: Net debt-free with net cash Rs 3,224 crore; net debt/equity -0.2x; sufficient cash to fund under-execution capex without borrowing
other.quote: We remain a net debt-free company with net cash of around Rs. 3,224 crores and a net debt-to-equity ratio of minus 0.2x.

guidance.statement: FY27 BESS commissioning target raised from 10 GWh to more than 12 GWh

margin.statement: Blended EBITDA margin 86.7% (renewable 90.8%, BESS 78.3%) in Q2 FY27
margin.quote: Our blended EBITDA margin was 86.7%, which comprises 90.8% from renewable generation and 78.3% from BESS operations, where the cost of power purchased to charge the batteries sits within the operating expenses.

order_book.statement: PPA signed portfolio at 92% of 8,370 MW contracted capacity after 430 MW FDRE PPAs in Q2 and 400 MW NTPC FDRE PPA

capex.quote: We have done around INR10,000 crores of capex this year till date. Roughly INR6,000 crores. So, INR6,500 crores is what we have done already, and I think we will do a similar amount or a higher amount in the second half of this year.

Further, CRISIL has upgraded ACME Solar Holdings rating outlook to AA- positive from AA- stable.

guidance.statement: Revenue expected to grow at 40% CAGR and EBITDA margin around 22% for FY27
guidance.quote: Going forward, we expect that our EBITDA level margin will be in and around 22% for FY27. Next slide, please. These are annual level performances. We have been consistently growing at 45% CAGR. Going forward also, our revenue is expected to grow at 40% CAGR. And at a margin level, we are very much sure that we will maintain our EBITDA level margin

guidance.statement: Order book will be healthy enough to sustain 40% CAGR guidance by year-end
guidance.quote: Going forward for balance six months, I can tell you that we will mop up the order which will be healthy enough to sustain our guidance forward.

demand.statement: Defence market size INR 4,000-5,000 crore over two years; company holds highest market share
demand.quote: In a ship building activity, that is including retrofit, new building and everything put together, we can safely say over a period of two years, the market size will be approximately ranging from INR 4,000 crore to INR 5,000 crore. And I already told you that we hold the highest market share.

demand.statement: Data centre opportunity large but no orders yet; guidance excludes data centre revenue until 2028
demand.quote: All our guidances are without a data centre, opportunity. So whatever guidance which we give you are without a data centre. So anything which comes out of data centre till 2028 will be addition or will be icing on the cake.

margin.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved to 13.5% from 11% despite commodity inflation
margin.quote: And despite of margin pressure from commodity inflation, we have been able to increase our EBITDA margin from 11% to 13.5%.

margin.statement: H2 margins typically higher due to larger operation size and product mix change
margin.quote: The margin in second half is generally higher. There are two reasons. The size of operation in H2 is generally higher as compared to H1, which helps us to absorb the fixed overhead in a better fashion. Plus, in the second half, there will be a certain change in product mix.

margin.statement: Import content reduced from 30%+ to single digit, ongoing margin improvement
margin.quote: When we started our journey about an AC plant, supplying an AC plant in an Indian naval platform, we had an import percentage of approximately 30 %-plus. Today, we brought it down to single digit. All these processes, all this kind of improvement, all kind of efficiency improvement will go on adding to the bottom line only.

order_book.statement: Order book at INR 200 crore as of September, started year at INR 270 crore
order_book.quote: Our order book position as of September is INR 200 crores. We started at INR 270 crores at the beginning of the year. Today, we are at INR 200 odd crores.

capex.statement: Small capex for Aquilon sub-zero chiller subsidiary
capex.quote: One very small thing happening in view of our new initiative in the sub-zero line, that is Aquilon, a small amount of CapEx may happen.

fund_raise.statement: May raise funds for new capacity if new opportunities arise; not needed for current 40% CAGR
fund_raise.quote: When we talk about a new capacity, new opportunity, which may need a fund also, so that time we probably will go to a market to raise a new fund also. But our earning call of 40% CAGR, as of today, we don't need a fund, neither we need a capacity, unless and until we see a new opportunity in the market.

risk.statement: No pending criminal cases against company, promoters or directors
risk.quote: No, no, no, no. Pending cases, there are no cases which was filed. Forget about pending cases, sir..

other.statement: Receivable days stable at 250 despite 84% revenue growth; target 200 days
other.quote: We have successfully brought it down to 250 days at March 26. And despite of 84 % revenue growth, we have been able to maintain that receivable days. Going forward, we will reduce those days to 200 days.

other.statement: Inventory increased from INR 54 cr to INR 80 cr for strategic sourcing against commodity inflation
other.quote: On a current asset, our inventories have been increased from INR 54 crores to INR 80 crores. That is a strategic procurement that has been done to ensure our EBITDA margins remain at an attractive level, plus to ensure that deliveries have been done in H2.

demand.statement: Primary market activity rebounded strongly in Q2 FY27 with INR 90,000 crores raised via IPOs and 90 lakh demat accounts added, up 14.2% YoY.

demand.statement: Total demat accounts in India crossed 24 crores; NSE unique investors reached 13.7 crores by September 2026.

margin.statement: Consolidated H1 FY27 total income INR 1,143.1 crores (+46.7% YoY), PAT INR 220.8 crores (+10.4% YoY); standalone net worth INR 2,263.4 crores.

order_book.statement: YUva and women's demat plans together account for ~45% of incremental demat account additions in Q2 FY27.

risk.statement: No specific guidance on market share recovery timeline; retail market share catch-up depends on new DP scaling and market conditions.

risk.statement: Expense normalization expected from next year as base effects kick in; negative operating leverage to ease after expense growth flattens.

other.statement: Supported SEBI's Project Jagruk investor awareness program; conducted 1,259 multilingual programs reaching 55,000+ participants across 10 states/UTs.

demand.statement: Pharma demand recovering with established API portfolio recovery and CDMO volume growth; new products ramping in H2
